# DECISION LOG — ARKALI GENESIS v2

Decisions taken during Phase 0 that are not large enough for an ADR, or that record a human ruling. Architectural decisions of consequence live in `docs/adr/ADR_INDEX.md`.

| # | Decision | Rationale | Authority |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-001 | 31 bounded contexts across a 7-layer model | Gives every canonical concern exactly one home and makes dependency direction mechanically checkable | Phase 0A |
| D-002 | Contexts consolidated into 4 architecture documents rather than one file per required artifact | The canonical set lists ~27 required 0A artifacts; coherent grouped documents beat 27 fragments that would drift apart | Phase 0A |
| D-003 | Layer rule: strictly-lower dependencies only, same-layer edges enumerated explicitly | An unenumerated same-layer edge is how cycles appear; making the 7 legitimate edges explicit makes the rest detectable | Phase 0A |
| D-004 | Promotion and rollback split across two lifecycle authorities | Prevents a failed promotion from approving its own recovery | ADR-0009 |
| D-005 | ID ranges allocated sparsely (MS 0001–0186, BP 0200–0243, VDC 0300–0380) | New requirements can be added inside their source block without renumbering; IDs are immutable | Phase 0B |
| D-006 | Minimise CONDITIONAL classification; everything else MANDATORY or OPTIONAL. Current count: **8** | Conditional classification is the main scope-narrowing exploit; every CONDITIONAL entry carries an objective machine-evaluable rule. The count is authoritative in `REQUIREMENT_REGISTER.md`, not here | Phase 0B (count revised by D-014) |
| D-007 | Architecture budgets set deliberately generous (400 logical lines, fan-out 12) | Purpose is catching a central orchestrator, not policing ordinary modules; tight budgets would generate GATE 8 noise | ADR-0008 |
| D-008 | Phase Gate Checker specified but **not** implemented in Phase 0 | Canonical phase model places implementation in Phase 2; Phase 0 produces no code | Phase 0B |
| D-009 | Golden Repair corpus **defined** but not populated | Corpus instances require an accepted Golden Product to inject into | Phase 0B |
| D-010 | Phase 0 commits as a candidate, explicitly not accepted | Canonical set forbids self-acceptance; commit records work, GATE 1 records acceptance | Phase 0B |
| D-011 | PyYAML used only to validate the authority map parses | Read-only validation of a Phase 0 artifact; no runtime dependency added, no lockfile, no install performed | Phase 0B |
| D-012 | Golden Repair: **definition** at Phase 0B, **instantiation** at Phase 30 | Derived from canonical text, not chosen: BP §Phase 0B says "corpus **definition**" and every sibling item in that list is a definition/specification/declaration/design; MS defines the corpus as "**injected** defects" executed "against a Golden Product revision that has already passed acceptance". Injection requires a target that does not exist before Phase 30 | HG1-02 correction |
| D-013 | Instantiation registered as new ARK-REQ-0187/0188 rather than by amending 0090/0091 | MS §Canonical Requirement Register makes IDs immutable and forbids reuse/renumbering. The reserved gap 0187–0199 in the MS block exists for exactly this | HG1-02 correction |
| D-014 | ARK-REQ-0012 reclassified CONDITIONAL → MANDATORY | MS §Frozen technology direction states "PostgreSQL-ready abstractions" unconditionally. The prior rule made the abstraction inapplicable in the default SQLite deployment — narrowing an unconditional requirement, the exact scope-reduction exploit the register exists to prevent | HG1-03 correction |
| D-015 | Verified *operation* on PostgreSQL is not registered as a requirement | No canonical statement requires it. Registering an unrequired obligation would be as wrong as omitting a required one | HG1-03 correction |
| D-016 | Contract inventory delivered at Phase 0A, not deferred to Phase 2 | BP §Phase 0A lists "contract inventory" explicitly. Phase 2 implements schemas; the inventory is architecture | HG1-01 correction |
| D-017 | Minimal stable-revision pointer primitive delivered **within** Phase 22B, owned by `lifecycle.release` | Recovery Supervisor needs an atomic pointer to a verified immutable revision, not the full release/supply-chain/deployment system. Placing the primitive in 22B removes the deadlock without weakening the rule that Self-Evolution cannot start before verified rollback exists, and without creating a second release authority | HG1-05 correction |
| D-018 | 22B prerequisites = 5, 6, 13, 20 (was 5, 20, 26) | 6 supplies immutable content-addressed revision identity; 13 supplies the "previously verified" record; 5/20 supply snapshot and restore proof. Full Phase 26 is not needed to verify rollback safety | HG1-05 correction |
| D-019 | Dependency validation must enumerate all four edge classes and ship a negative control | The original check used explicit prerequisites only and reported "no cycles" while a real deadlock existed. An edge class omitted from a graph check is a false negative by construction | HG1-05 correction |
| D-020 | Contract definition phase separated from implementation phase | C-03 was required by Phase 2 while implemented at Phase 5 — an impossible forward prerequisite. Phase 2 needs the schema/interface, not the runtime | HG1-06 correction |
| D-021 | Deliverable counts parsed from the canonical Build Protocol lists, never hand-entered | *(historical defect)* an earlier audit read `12/12` while other artifacts read `11/11`, because one canonical bullet had been split into two rows. Current derived counts are 0A 16/16, 0B 11/11 | HG1-08 correction |
| D-022 | Derived numbers are computed at check time, not transcribed | Three artifacts held stale denominators after the register was corrected, including the audit asserting all artifacts agreed. Same root cause as F-0002 | HG1-07 / HG1-09 correction |

## Human rulings incorporated (recorded, not decided here)

| Ruling | Source | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **The recovery route was derived from the canonical relation, not chosen** | Phase 7 Package 3 | `EXECUTION_AND_CAPABILITY.md` §3 says a `RUNNING` job without a live heartbeat "transitions to `RECOVERABLE`, then `RESUMING`". The canonical `Job` relation declares no `RUNNING → RECOVERABLE` edge and `evaluate` refuses it — verified mechanically before a line was written. The prose names the states a crashed job resolves **to**; `STATE_MACHINES.md` §3 owns the **edges** it travels. The only declared route is `RUNNING → FAILED → RECOVERABLE`, which is exactly the disposition Package 2 already owns, so the sweep **composes** that path instead of repeating it. No canonical document is in error and the machine was not modified — the appearance of conflict came from reading the prose as an edge list |
| **`RESUMING` is shared because the relation says so, not because Package 3 arranged it** | Phase 7 Package 3 | `RESUMING` has exactly two predecessors, `PAUSED` and `RECOVERABLE`. Pause and crash recovery therefore converge on one lifecycle meaning as a property of the canonical machine. No pause-specific or recovery-specific resuming state exists, no `is_resuming` flag exists, and a control derives the predecessor set from the relation so a canonical change to it fails the suite rather than silently widening the sweep |
| **Pause leaves the attempt open; crash recovery closes it** | Phase 7 Package 3 | The asymmetry is the whole design. A paused execution is *suspended*: closing its attempt would consume a retry, and pausing is not failing; extending its deadline would reset the timeout basis the job was admitted under. A crashed execution is *gone*: closing its attempt is what makes the departed owner unable to act, since a closed attempt refuses every write and a returning zombie worker cannot heartbeat, complete or fail it. The consumed attempt is honest accounting — it really happened and really stopped |
| **The sweep filters on `RUNNING`, and that filter is load-bearing** | Phase 7 Package 3 | A paused job also holds an open attempt and is deliberately silent, so selecting by open-attempt staleness alone would "recover" every paused job. Reading a recorded state to decide which rows to *consider* is not deciding where a job *goes*; the machine still evaluates every move, and the AST control distinguishes the comparison from an assignment — a substring check could not, and was replaced when it produced a false positive on that very line |
| **An unregistered job type raises rather than defaulting** | Phase 7 Package 3 | An absent declaration is an unanswered question. Returning `False` would be a declaration nobody made and returning `True` would grant a capability nobody declared, so `supports_pause` raises `UnknownJobType`. Governing rule 7 resolves an unwaived unevaluable rule to APPLICABLE, so building the registry was never optional — `ARK-REQ-0060` could not be avoided by declining to make it answerable |
| **The registry is joined by the natural key, with no foreign key** | Phase 7 Package 3 | A foreign key from `durable_job.job_type` would make registration a *precondition of submitting*, which is admission control — C-21 at Phase 8. The type instead fails closed at the point its capability is asked about. Declaration is write-once so a job in flight keeps the capability its type was declared with |
| **A control was scoped to one file and could not fire; it was replaced, not deleted** | Phase 7 Package 3 | Package 2's `test_the_execution_module_never_enters_resuming` read `execution.py` alone. Package 3 implemented `RESUMING`, `PAUSED` and `supports_pause` in two other modules of the same context and the control **still passed** — verified against the finished tree before it was touched. Deleting a control that started failing needs a fires-for-the-right-reason proof; this one needed the opposite proof, that it could not fire at all. The replacement derives, over the whole context, which modules request `RESUMING`, requires every use of the name to be a transition target, and proves the Package 2 dispositions have no path to it |
| **The engine-neutrality control was strengthened, not widened, to admit `Boolean`** | Phase 7 Package 3 | The old check compared type names against a hand-written whitelist over three hand-named tables — so `JobTypeRecord` escaped it entirely, and `Boolean` would have needed adding to a list. Both halves were derived instead: the record set comes from the mapped classes, and the real assertion is that every column's type lives in SQLAlchemy's generic type namespace, which catches any `sqlalchemy.dialects` type whether or not anyone listed it. A dialect-specific type was injected as a mutation and caught |
| **The canonical Job machine was sufficient; nothing was added to it** | Phase 7 Package 2 | Checked before implementing, not after: `RUNNING→FAILED`, `FAILED→{RECOVERABLE, DEAD_LETTER}` and `RUNNING→CANCELLED` express every Package 2 semantic. No state, transition or recovery edge was invented, and three properties are consequences of the canonical relation rather than of code — `DEAD_LETTER` has no outgoing transition, so a dead-lettered job cannot be retried at all; `CANCELLED` is reachable only from `RUNNING`, so a queued job cannot be cancelled and a terminal one cannot be cancelled twice |
| **Retry accounting is rows, never a counter** | Phase 7 Package 2 | A column would be settable, resettable and free to drift from what happened; `count(job_execution_attempt)` cannot be any of those. The primary key (`job_id`, `attempt`) is therefore also the concurrency backstop, proven by inserting a duplicate attempt past the service and being refused by the database. A control fails on any column whose name reads like a running tally |
| **The deadline is an absolute instant, not a remaining duration** | Phase 7 Package 2 | A remaining-duration counter silently restarts with the process, which is precisely the failure durability exists to prevent. `deadline_at` is computed once when the attempt opens and asserted unchanged across a reopen; a control fails if the column stops being a `DateTime` |
| **Package 2 disposes to RECOVERABLE and stops there** | Phase 7 Package 2 | `RECOVERABLE → RESUMING` is the entry to resumption, and resumption is Package 3. Package 2 therefore decides only *whether* another attempt is permitted and records it as a canonical state; a control fails if `RESUMING`, `PAUSED` or `supports_pause` appears in the module. Where a second attempt had to be exercised at all, the *test* moves the job through `RESUMING` using the canonical machine — the implementation never asks for it |
| **`owner` is recorded, never chosen** | Phase 7 Package 2 | Refusing a stale owner is a durability property and belongs here. Selecting, allocating or balancing owners is C-21 at Phase 8; a control fails on the vocabulary (`admit`, `claim`, `lease`, `allocate`, `worker_pool`, `resource_budget`, …), and it caught an injected `allocate()` during mutation testing |
| **State names moved into the authority module rather than the control being relaxed** | Phase 7 Package 2 | Package 2 must name a target to request a declared move, which would have put a second copy of the vocabulary in the context and broken Package 1's no-state-literal control. The alternative — exempting the new module — would have weakened a control to fit the code. Instead `job_state_machine.py` exports named constants resolved through `DEFINITION.states`, so a state the machine stops declaring is a KeyError at import, and the requesting module imports the name. The control is unchanged and still passes |
| **Three mutations exposed real control gaps, and the controls were strengthened** | Phase 7 Package 2 | Replacing the disposition's `transition(...)` with a direct `lifecycle_state = ...` left every behavioural test green, because the value written was one the machine would have allowed anyway — so a control now asserts that the lifecycle column is assigned in exactly one method, derived as the one that calls `evaluate`. Dropping `_guard` from a *private* method was missed because the guard sweep only examined public methods of one class; it now covers every class and every method in the context, keyed on session *operations* rather than session mentions, so a constructor that merely holds a session is not a false positive. 14/14 mutations caught after the repair |
| **Both new test modules were decomposed rather than exempted** | Phase 7 Package 2 | The 400-line budget fired on `test_durable_execution.py` (546) and `test_durable_authority.py` (415). ADR-0008 decomposition: a shared `durable_harness.py` and `durable_reader.py` plus two test modules each, following the `typescript_reader.py` and `plane_harness.py` precedents. No exception requested, no check relaxed |
| **"Workflow Core" in the matrix row title carries no Phase 7 obligation** | Phase 7 Package 1 | `IMPLEMENTATION_DEPENDENCY_MATRIX.md` row 7 reads "Durable Job + Workflow Core", but its Contracts column names **C-19 only**, every Phase 7 register row is owned by `execution.durable`, and every `execution.workflow` requirement (0062–0065, 0328, 0329, 0332) plus C-20 is **Phase 17**. Read against the register and the inventory, Phase 7 builds no workflow functionality. Recorded here so the narrowing is a stated reading of authority rather than a silent omission |
| **Two identities, one store — idempotency is a constraint, not a second table** | Phase 7 Package 1 | `job_id` answers "which row is this?" and (`job_type`, `idempotency_key`) answers "has this work already been submitted?". A separate idempotency table would be a second place answering the same question, which `MS §Constitution 1` forbids. `uq_durable_job_idempotency` is the authority; the lookup in `submit` only turns a repeat into a typed result. Proven by writing the row directly past the service and being refused by the database |
| **Idempotency keys are scoped by job type** | Phase 7 Package 1 | A global key space would let one producer suppress another's job by reusing a string. The same key under two job types is two pieces of work |
| **No column was added for a behaviour that does not exist** | Phase 7 Package 1 | `MS §Durable Runtime` names heartbeat, retries, timeout and dead-letter, and it would have been easy to add the columns now "for later". A column present for an unimplemented behaviour is a claim, and C-19 is STRICT, which permits adding optional fields later with a defined absent-value meaning. Package 1 therefore ships the three records it actually implements and nothing else |
| **The kernel error fan-in budget fired again, and the Phase 6 decomposition was completed rather than extended** | Phase 7 Package 1 | Adding `execution/durable/errors.py` took `kernel.contracts.errors` to a fan-in of 16 against a budget of 15 — the same budget Phase 6 Package 1 hit. `control/architecture/refusal.py` already existed for exactly this and its own docstring named **three** modules, but only one had been routed through it, leaving the fan-in at exactly 15 with no headroom. Routing `authority_map.py` (8 raise sites) and `gates/runner.py` (2) through the context factory takes it to 14. Same exception type, message and source; only the edge count changes. ADR-0008 decomposition, no GATE 8 exception requested |
| **The durable-surface tripwire was proved to fire before it was touched** | Phase 7 Package 1 | `test_surfaces_not_yet_built_are_still_absent` asserted that nothing existed under `execution/durable`. The first three real modules made it fail, naming all three and stating the obligation. Only after that obligation was met — injected PEP, every governed operation guarded, a real denying PDP proving refusal — was the assertion replaced. The replacement is **stronger**: it derives which execution packages are built and requires each to consult a PEP, so it keeps failing for the next unenforced package instead of going quiet forever the moment something exists. Phase 5 Package 4 precedent; not a finding |
| **Two controls were strengthened because mutation testing showed they measured the wrong thing** | Phase 7 Package 1 | The engine-construction control checked call sites only, so `create_engine` could sit imported one keystroke from use — the import is now refused too. The PEP-coverage control searched for the string `PolicyEnforcementPoint`, which no single edit could defeat; it now requires a decision method to be **called on a PEP**, after a first attempt matched `self._machine.evaluate(...)` because the state machine shares the method name. Both were found by mutations that MISSED, and both mutations were kept |
| **A bad mutation is not evidence** | Phase 7 Package 1 | Three of twelve mutations initially missed. Two were semantic no-ops — an unused import, and an alias that left the searched string in place — and one targeted the wrong test subject. They were corrected and re-run rather than recorded as gaps or as passes; the final round is 12/12 caught with every file digest-verified as restored |
| **Acceptance is declared, never inferred — the F-0025 shape applied to phase status** | pre-Phase-7 governance repair | F-0025 already established the rule for findings: state comes from a declared cell, prose has no effect, unreadable input is refused. The phase-status parser had never been brought under it and still decided acceptance by substring. The repair reuses that shape rather than inventing a second one — `parse_declared_state` reads the leading declared segment, resolves it against a vocabulary taken off the rows that actually exist, and refuses anything unknown or self-contradictory. `GovernanceState` remains the sole acceptance authority; no second model was created |
| **The vocabulary was read off the live rows; no document was rewritten to fit the parser** | pre-Phase-7 governance repair | Every phase-status cell in `BUILD_STATE.md` already begins with a bolded declared state — `**MACHINE-ACCEPTED**`, `**UNLOCKED — NOT_STARTED**`, `**ACCEPTED — HUMAN GATE 1 granted**`. The parser was made to understand that existing syntax rather than a new one, so backward compatibility is a property of the design and not a migration. Verified over all ten live rows before and after: **no phase changed meaning** |
| **Acceptance requires an affirmative head; absence of a negation grants nothing** | pre-Phase-7 governance repair | The predecessor's second mistake mattered more than the first. Even scoped to a single cell, `has ACCEPTED and not has NOT ACCEPTED` accepts every unrecognised state that happens to contain the token. `grants_acceptance` is now a two-member whitelist, so an unknown state can only ever be refused — never accepted by default |
| **A qualifier may narrow a state; it may never reverse it** | pre-Phase-7 governance repair | `UNLOCKED — IN PROGRESS, NOT ACCEPTED` is a legitimate narrowing and must parse. `MACHINE-ACCEPTED — NOT ACCEPTED` is a contradiction, and choosing which half to believe is exactly how a governance parser starts inventing state. Both contradictory forms are **refused**, which is the strict side |
| **The row that caused the defect is written plainly again, as the live proof** | pre-Phase-7 governance repair | Phase 6's acceptance was recorded with Phase 7's row deliberately contorted to dodge the parser — a workaround, not a fix, and the second such dodge in this repository (F-0029's note was the first). The natural wording, "Both prerequisites, Phases 5 and 6, are accepted", is restored. The predecessor rule still reads it as accepting Phase 7; the repaired parser reads `UNLOCKED`. A governance document should be written for its readers, not around its parser |
| **Two adjacent instances of the same habit were repaired with it, and one dead property was fixed rather than deleted** | pre-Phase-7 governance repair | `is_locked` returned `"LOCKED" in status_text`, so every `UNLOCKED` row reported itself locked; it had **no caller**, which is the only reason it never surfaced. `check_handoff.py` decided unlockedness by the same prose search. Both now read the declared state. The dead property was corrected rather than removed, because the next caller would have inherited the bug and the correction costs one line |
| **F-0035 was repaired in the document, not in the Protected Core parser** | pre-Phase-7 governance repair | Blank lines had split the findings table so that F-0027…F-0034 were invisible to `stopping_findings` — found because F-0034 was opened as HIGH and the gate still reported none open. `findings.py`'s table detection is correct for a well-formed document and is Protected Core; the defect was layout. The blank lines were removed, no row content was touched, and a derived control now fails if any row shaped like a finding is missing from `parse_findings`, so the fragility cannot silently return |
| **F-0034 is HIGH because of what it could do, not because of what it did** | pre-Phase-7 governance repair | Mechanically it is F-0025 (a governance parser deciding state by substring, failing open), which was MEDIUM. But its blast radius is the acceptance decision itself: `checker.check_prerequisites` reads the same property, so an unimplemented phase could have satisfied a later phase's prerequisite. F-0024 established that acceptance asserted without being earned is HIGH. Severity follows the consequence class. That no phase was actually falsely accepted in a recorded verdict is recorded as mitigation, not used to discount the severity |
| **No re-score of Phase 6 was performed or required** | pre-Phase-7 governance repair | GOV-001 governs *re-scoring an accepted phase*. The gate was not run for Phase 6, no verdict was recorded, and `phase_6_report.json` and `phase_6_traceability.json` are byte-unchanged. Backward-compatibility parsing proves Phase 6 remains MACHINE-ACCEPTED under the repaired parser, so its recorded verdict is not disturbed. This follows the F-0026/F-0027/F-0028 precedent of a governance repair performed between phases without authorization, because nothing is being re-scored |
| **C-15 is traced through ARK-REQ-0004, because it has no register row of its own** | Phase 6 Package 3 | `CONTRACT_INVENTORY.md` assigns both C-14 and C-15 to Phase 6, while the register assigns all three Phase 6 requirements to `evidence.artifact`. Read literally that leaves the audit chain implemented and untraced — a whole Protected Core subsystem discharging nothing. ARK-REQ-0004's statement is that the Evidence Plane **components** exist, which is the row C-15 belongs to, so `phase_6_traceability.json` claims both contracts under it and names evidence for each. Nothing in the register was amended: the mapping is recorded in the traceability record, which is where a phase explains what its claim rests on |
| **The gap in that mapping's enforcement is reported, not papered over** | Phase 6 Package 3 | Check C6 requires a SATISFIED claim to *name* an implementation and an evidence source; it has no per-contract granularity, so deleting the C-15 half of ARK-REQ-0004's evidence would still be accepted. That was proven mechanically as case D2 of the acceptance-guard run rather than assumed. **No control was added.** No accepted traceability record — Phases 2, 3, 4 or 5 — names a contract id at all, so a repository-wide rule demanding one would fail four accepted phases, and rewriting accepted evidence to satisfy a new rule is exactly what GOV-001 exists to prevent. Strengthening the traceability contract is an Acceptance Engine change and belongs to Phase 13 |
| **`prov` was resolved from canonical authority, not treated as prose** | Phase 6 Package 3 | The register's Evidence keys define `prov` as provenance evidence and `VDC §Provenance` fixes its content — hash, producer/task, provider/model, spec version, context hash, parents, normalization, tests and evidence, with `MS §Artifact Fabric` adding timestamps. Every `prov` claim is therefore discharged by a real persisted recording of those items against real bytes, re-read after the database is closed and a **new engine** opened, never by a paragraph asserting that provenance exists |
| **ARK-REQ-0349's subject is a Phase 6 test artifact, and no release was fabricated** | Phase 6 Package 3 | "Critical generated/release artifacts" names a class of artifact, not a release event. Manufacturing a fake release manifest to demonstrate the provenance contract would have pulled Phase 26 (C-31, SBOM, signing) forward and produced evidence about something that does not exist. What is claimed is that the contract records the canonical metadata and binds it to an immutable content-addressed identity that survives a reopen; what is not claimed is that any release artifact has been produced |
| **Graph readiness is asserted; no graph is built** | Phase 6 Package 3 | `VERIFICATION_ARCHITECTURE.md` §2.2 rules 1–3 are storage properties Phase 6 owns — stable artifact identity, evidence referencing it, supersession preserving history, no structurally orphaned record. §2.3 coverage is C-16 at Phase 13. The controls assert only the former, so a later graph remains possible without Phase 6 computing a single coverage figure |
| **A tripwire fired against this package's own evidence and the evidence changed, not the tripwire** | Phase 6 Package 3 | The first draft of the integration module was 463 logical lines against a 400-line budget and used a banned substitution marker in a docstring. Both are structure-validator checks doing their job. The budget was answered by decomposition per ADR-0008 — `plane_harness.py` plus two test modules, following the `typescript_reader.py` precedent — and the marker by rewording. Neither check was relaxed and no exception was requested |
| **An assertion that compared a driver representation was restated, not deleted** | Phase 6 Package 3 | Proving a superseded record is unchanged first failed on `recorded_at`: SQLite returns a naive datetime for a `DateTime(timezone=True)` column, which `integrity._render` normalises to UTC precisely so the digest cannot depend on it. The assertion was testing the driver. It now compares the canonical digest payload and every digested field — the contract's own definition of "unchanged" — which is stronger than the original, not weaker |
| **The F-0029 phase-status trap was triggered while recording this acceptance, and caught by re-deriving rather than by assuming** | Phase 6 Package 3 | F-0029's record noted a trap it had avoided: `PhaseStatus.is_accepted` matches the substring `ACCEPTED` anywhere in a status cell, excluding only the spaced form `NOT ACCEPTED`. Writing Phase 7's new row as "…Phases 5 and 6, **are accepted**…" made `GovernanceState` report **Phase 7 itself as accepted**, and `check_handoff`'s unlocked-phase derivation resolve to `None`. A second wording that named the parser's own identifier reproduced it, because the identifier contains the token. Found by re-deriving the governed state after writing it, which is why that step exists. The cell was reworded; **the parser was not changed** — it is `acceptance.engine`, Protected Core, and altering it after the Phase 6 verdict was recorded would modify the accepted change set. The fragility is real and belongs to a phase that owns the Acceptance Engine, not to a post-acceptance edit here |
| **F-0033 was found by running the tier the way the report records it** | Phase 6 Package 3 | `python -m pytest tests/persistence -q` failed standalone while `python -m pytest -q` passed, because `PersistenceBase.metadata` is populated by import side effect. That made Alembic's autogenerate target one table out of seven — a tool configured to propose dropping six real tables. The fix is at the migration composition root and **not** in `kernel.persistence`: the kernel is rank 0 and the record modules are rank 1 and rank 2, so a kernel-side registry would be a forbidden dependency direction. `env.py` is tooling outside `backend/arkali`, and three derived controls now fail if it omits, over-declares or fails to import a mapped module |
| HUMAN GATE 8 ratified | human authority | Architecture-budget exception is a human gate |
| Direct-AI benchmark states | human authority | `NOT_CONFIGURED` / verified `EXTERNAL_UNAVAILABLE` do not block release; never fabricate an external PASS |
| Phase 0 split 0A/0B | human authority | Two parts, one acceptance package, one gate |
| Workflow derived caches | human authority | Permitted when deterministically derived, hash-bound and invalidated |
| ROLLBACK_STABLE constraints | human authority | Recovery-Supervisor-only, verified immutable target, atomic pointer switch preferred, no transformation |
| Autonomy model | human authority | Machine acceptance for normal phases; stop only at the 8 gates or a failed machine gate |
| **ERR-001 governance erratum** | human authority | `engineering.import` physical `module_root` → `backend/arkali/engineering/project_import`. Physical realizability only: logical identity, authority, lifecycle, TRUST, Protected Core membership and requirement meaning unchanged. Phase 0 not reopened; Stable Core semantics not invoked (no Stable Core exists). Closes F-0015 |
| **Handoff protocol institutionalised** | Phase 2 follow-up | `ARKALI_HANDOFF.md` + `ARKALI_NEW_SESSION_PROMPT.txt` + `scripts/check_handoff.py`. The manifest is an index, never a second authority; every claim it makes is mechanically compared against repository truth and any disagreement is `HANDOFF_DRIFT`. Refresh is mandatory after each accepted phase, gate decision, erratum, promotion, rollback, new BLOCKER/HIGH or change of NEXT EXACT ACTION |
| **HUMAN GATE 1 ACCEPTED** | human authority | Phase 0A + 0B accepted as one package on candidate `007ebf6`; 9 ADRs PROPOSED → ACCEPTED; Phase 1 unlocked. Recorded as `HGR-001`. Autonomous progression through normal phases now applies until GATE 2 (Phase 23) or an earlier gate condition |
| Isolation Backend abstraction | human authority | Properties, not technologies; unsatisfiable ⇒ UNSUPPORTED/DENY; never silently downgrade |
| **State-machine primitive placed in `kernel.contracts`** | Phase 3 implementation | The twelve machines are owned by ten contexts, three of them in the `control` layer. `allow_same_layer: false` means a shared primitive in `control.architecture` could not be imported by `control.registry.project` or `control.registry.provider`. Only layer rank 0 is reachable from every authority, so the *mechanism* is a kernel contract while every *machine* stays owned by the context the authority map names. No universal state-machine object exists |
| **Executable machine definitions are the implementation authority** | Phase 3 implementation | `STATE_MACHINES.md` remains the canonical specification; the twelve executable definitions are the implementation authority for their own machines. Ownership is stated in each module rather than left implicit, and the two are reconciled mechanically on every run, so neither can become a silent private copy of the other |
| **Canonical §6 read literally, not narrowed** | Phase 3 implementation | `any→QUARANTINED` in `STATE_MACHINES.md` §6 is implemented exactly as written, which leaves Plugin Lifecycle with no terminal state. Recorded as F-0018 for human ruling. An implementing actor narrowing a canonical document to something more sensible is precisely the reinterpretation the constitution forbids |
| **ERR-004 — F-0024 confirmed; ARK-REQ-0111 implemented, not reclassified** | human authority | The human ruling refused reclassification, deferral and any weakening of the evidence requirements. The stronger Protected Core profile is now executable in `acceptance.engine`, derives its categories from MS §Protected Core and its membership from `AUTHORITY_MAP`, and cannot be declared or downgraded by the actor making the change. Applied to its own remediation candidate |
